question:
Who sent the Greek ambassador Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Seleucus
Tolmi
Dionysus
Sikandar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Seleucus

Explanation:
Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by Seleucus Nicator (a general of Alexander and founder of the Seleucid Empire). This historical event occurred around 305-303 BCE after a war between Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus, followed by a treaty. As per the treaty, Seleucus ceded eastern territories (modern-day Afghanistan and Balochistan) to Chandragupta in exchange for 500 war elephants. Megasthenes wrote 'Indica', which provides a detailed account of the Mauryan Empire's social, economic, and administrative systems.

Extra Facts:
Megasthenes described the grandeur of Pataliputra (modern Patna), the efficiency of Mauryan administration, and various social classes. According to him, Chandragupta's rule was centralized and disciplined. Indica was the first major text to introduce India to the Greek world, though the original work is lost, its content is known through citations by other Greek writers.

question_hi:
चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के दरबार में यूनानी राजदूत मेगस्थनीज को किसने भेजा था?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options_hi: सेल्यूकस
टॉलमी
डायोनिसस
सिकंदर
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है सेल्यूकस

Explanation:
मेगस्थनीज एक यूनानी राजदूत था जिसे सेल्यूकस निकेटर (सिकंदर के सेनापति और सेल्यूकस साम्राज्य के संस्थापक) ने चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के दरबार में भेजा था। यह ऐतिहासिक घटना 305-303 ईसा पूर्व के आसपास हुई, जब चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य और सेल्यूकस के बीच युद्ध हुआ और बाद में एक संधि हुई। इस संधि के तहत सेल्यूकस ने पूर्वी क्षेत्र (आधुनिक अफगानिस्तान और बलूचिस्तान) चंद्रगुप्त को दे दिए और बदले में 500 हाथी प्राप्त किए। मेगस्थनीज ने अपनी पुस्तक 'इंडिका' में मौर्य साम्राज्य की सामाजिक, आर्थिक और प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था का विस्तृत विवरण दिया है।

Extra Facts:
मेगस्थनीज ने पाटलिपुत्र (आधुनिक पटना) की भव्यता, मौर्य प्रशासन की दक्षता और समाज के विभिन्न वर्गों के बारे में लिखा। उसके अनुसार, चंद्रगुप्त का शासन केंद्रीकृत और अनुशासित था। इंडिका यूनानी दुनिया को भारत के बारे में जानकारी देने वाला पहला प्रमुख ग्रंथ था, हालाँकि मूल पुस्तक खो गई है, लेकिन अन्य यूनानी लेखकों के उद्धरणों से इसकी जानकारी मिलती है।

question:
Who, with the help of Kautilya, overthrew Dhanananda, the last Nanda ruler, in 322 BC?

[SSC MTS ]
options: Ashoka
Chandragupta Maurya
Akbar
Kalashoka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chandragupta Maurya

Explanation:
In 322 BCE, Chandragupta Maurya, with the assistance of his mentor Kautilya (Chanakya), defeated Dhanananda, the last ruler of the Nanda Dynasty. This victory led to the establishment of the Mauryan Empire, India's first major empire. Kautilya authored the Arthashastra, a seminal text on statecraft and administration. Chandragupta's reign marked a turning point in Indian history, introducing a centralized administrative system.

Extra Facts:
The Mauryan Empire (322–185 BCE) was the first pan-Indian empire. Chandragupta also defeated Seleucus Nicator, securing territories in the northwest. His grandson, Ashoka, embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War and promoted it widely.

अकबर
कालाशोक
solution_hi:

Explanation:
322 ईसा पूर्व में, चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य ने अपने गुरु कौटिल्य (चाणक्य) की सहायता से नंद वंश के अंतिम शासक धनानंद को पराजित किया। इस विजय के बाद चंद्रगुप्त ने मौर्य साम्राज्य की स्थापना की, जो भारत का पहला विशाल साम्राज्य था। कौटिल्य ने अर्थशास्त्र नामक ग्रंथ लिखा, जो राजनीति और शासन प्रबंधन का महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत है। चंद्रगुप्त का शासनकाल भारतीय इतिहास में एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ था, जिसने केन्द्रीकृत प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था को मजबूत किया।

Extra Facts:
मौर्य साम्राज्य (322-185 ईसा पूर्व) भारत का पहला साम्राज्य था जिसने अधिकांश भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप पर शासन किया। चंद्रगुप्त ने सेल्यूकस निकेटर को भी हराकर पश्चिमी क्षेत्रों पर अधिकार किया। उनके पोते अशोक ने कलिंग युद्ध के बाद बौद्ध धर्म अपनाया और इसे फैलाया।

question:
The author of ‘Arthashastra’ was a contemporary of which of the following rulers?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Chandragupta Maurya
Samudragupta
Chandragupta Vikramaditya
Ashoka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chandragupta Maurya

Explanation:
The author of Arthashastra was Chanakya (Kautilya), who was a contemporary of Chandragupta Maurya. Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in 322 BCE, and Chanakya served as his prime minister and mentor. The Arthashastra is an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economics, military strategy, and governance. It is a crucial source for understanding the Mauryan administration.

Extra Facts:
Chanakya is also known as Vishnugupta and Kautilya. He played a key role in overthrowing the Nanda dynasty and installing Chandragupta Maurya as the ruler. The Arthashastra consists of 15 books and 180 chapters, providing detailed knowledge on governance, diplomacy, law, and economy.

question:
Who among the following deciphered the Brahmi Script of the Mauryan period?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: James Mill
James Prinsep
Rakhal Das Banerji
Herbert Hope Risley
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is James Prinsep

Explanation:
James Prinsep, a British archaeologist and linguist, successfully deciphered the Brahmi script of the Mauryan period in 1837. His work was instrumental in reading the Brahmi inscriptions on Ashoka's edicts, which provided crucial insights into the Mauryan Empire and Emperor Ashoka. Prinsep studied various inscriptions and coins to understand the structure of the Brahmi script, marking a significant milestone in Indian history and archaeology.

Extra Facts:
The Brahmi script is one of the oldest scripts in India and is considered the ancestor of many modern Indian scripts, including Devanagari. Ashoka's edicts, written in Brahmi, offer valuable information about Buddhism and Mauryan administration. James Prinsep's decipherment of Brahmi was a groundbreaking achievement in Indian archaeology.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से किसने मौर्य काल की ब्राह्मी लिपि का कूटवाचन (deciphered) किया?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: जेम्स मिल (James Mill)
जेम्स प्रिंसेप (James Prinsep)
राखल दास बनर्जी (Rakhal Das Banerji)
हर्बर्ट होपरिस्ली (Herbert Hope Risley)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है जेम्स प्रिंसेप (James Prinsep)

Explanation:
जेम्स प्रिंसेप, एक ब्रिटिश पुरातत्वविद् और भाषाविद्, ने 1837 में मौर्य काल की ब्राह्मी लिपि को सफलतापूर्वक कूटवाचित (deciphered) किया। उन्होंने अशोक के शिलालेखों पर उत्कीर्ण ब्राह्मी लिपि को पढ़ने में महत्वपूर्ण योगदान दिया। यह खोज भारतीय इतिहास और पुरातत्व के लिए एक मील का पत्थर साबित हुई, क्योंकि इससे मौर्य साम्राज्य और सम्राट अशोक के बारे में महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी प्राप्त हुई। प्रिंसेप ने अपने शोध के लिए विभिन्न शिलालेखों और सिक्कों का अध्ययन किया, जिससे ब्राह्मी लिपि की संरचना को समझने में मदद मिली।

Extra Facts:
ब्राह्मी लिपि भारत की सबसे प्राचीन लिपियों में से एक है और यह देवनागरी सहित कई आधुनिक भारतीय लिपियों की जननी मानी जाती है। अशोक के शिलालेखों में इस लिपि का प्रयोग किया गया था, जो बौद्ध धर्म और मौर्य प्रशासन के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान करते हैं। जेम्स प्रिंसेप की यह उपलब्धि भारतीय पुरातत्व के इतिहास में एक महत्वपूर्ण घटना थी।

question:
Identify the Mauryan king who gave up conquest after winning a war.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Dashratha
Chandragupta Maurya
Bindusara
Ashoka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ashoka

Explanation:
Emperor Ashoka renounced conquest after the Kalinga War (261 BCE). The war was so devastating that it deeply affected Ashoka, leading him to adopt 'Dhamma Vijaya' (victory through righteousness) and propagate Buddhism. He promoted non-violence, tolerance, and ethical living through his edicts and pillars. Ashoka's reign is considered the golden age of the Mauryan Empire.

Extra Facts:
Ashoka spread Buddhism across his empire and sent missionaries abroad. His edicts were inscribed in the Brahmi script, an important ancient Indian writing system. The 'Ashoka Chakra' in the Indian flag is inspired by his emblem.

Explanation:

He authored the treatise 'Arthashastra', a comprehensive text on politics, economics, military strategy, and governance. It was written during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Mauryan Empire. Arthashastra is considered the most significant political treatise of ancient India, providing detailed policies for statecraft.

Extra Facts:
Kautilya assisted Chandragupta Maurya in defeating the Nanda ruler Dhana Nanda and played a crucial role in establishing the Mauryan Empire. question:
Ashoka the Great, belonged to the:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Gupta Dynasty
Shunga Dynasty
Maurya Dynasty
Chola Dynasty
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Maurya Dynasty

Explanation:
Emperor Ashoka the Great (273-232 BCE) belonged to the Maurya Dynasty of ancient India. He was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya and son of Bindusara. After the Kalinga War (261 BCE), Ashoka embraced Buddhism and propagated Dhamma. He erected pillar edicts and rock edicts across India and Asia, describing his governance and moral principles. His reign is considered the golden age of the Mauryan Empire.

Extra Facts:
The Mauryan Empire (322-185 BCE) was India's first major empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya. Arthashastra (by Kautilya/Chanakya) is a key political treatise from this era. Ashoka used the Brahmi script in his inscriptions, which became the basis for modern Indian scripts.

Explanation:

Extra Facts:
Ashoka's edicts were inscribed in the Brahmi script and written in Prakrit language. They emphasize religious tolerance, animal welfare, and administrative reforms. After the Kalinga War, Ashoka promoted Buddhism and sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka for its propagation.

solution:

Explanation:
Chandragupta Maurya defeated Dhana Nanda to establish the Maurya dynasty. Extra Facts:
The Nanda dynasty was a powerful dynasty of Magadha, founded by Mahapadma Nanda . During Dhana Nanda's rule, heavy taxation led to widespread public discontent. Chanakya used this dissatisfaction to help Chandragupta rise to power.

question:
The ambassador who was sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by the Greek ruler Seleucus Nicator is ____.

solution:

Explanation:
Seleucus Nicator, one of Alexander's successors, sent Megasthenes as an ambassador to the court of Chandragupta Maurya. Megasthenes wrote the book 'Indica', which provides a detailed account of the social, economic, and administrative systems of the Mauryan Empire. This book is a crucial source for understanding ancient Indian history. After the war between Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus Nicator, a treaty was signed under which Seleucus gave his daughter in marriage to Chandragupta and ceded some territories, while Chandragupta gifted him 500 elephants.

Extra Facts:
Megasthenes' 'Indica' is the only foreign source that offers detailed information about the Mauryan period. He described the grandeur of Pataliputra, the efficiency of Mauryan administration, and the caste system in Indian society. Although some of his observations are exaggerated, this text remains historically invaluable.

question:
One of the major events of Ashoka’s reign was the convening of the ______ Buddhist Sangha (council) in 250 BCE in the capital Pataliputra.

[SSC CGL 2020]
options: First
Fourth
Third
Second
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Third

Explanation:
During the reign of Emperor Ashoka (273-232 BCE), the Third Buddhist Council was convened in 250 BCE at Pataliputra. This council was presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa. Its main objective was to resolve disputes within Buddhism and to purify the Buddhist texts. After this council, Ashoka sent his son Mahinda and daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism. This event marked a significant turning point in the history of the Mauryan Empire.

Extra Facts:
Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War (261 BCE) and adopted the policy of Dhamma. He erected pillar edicts and rock edicts across India and beyond to propagate Buddhism. The Third Buddhist Council played a crucial role in the widespread dissemination of Buddhism, transforming it into a global religion.

question:
The foundation of the Mauryan empire was laid by________

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Kalashoka
Chandragupta Maurya
Bindusara
Ashoka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chandragupta Maurya

Explanation:
The foundation of the Mauryan Empire was laid by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE. He defeated the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, Dhana Nanda, and established his rule over Magadha. With the guidance of his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya), Chandragupta built a vast empire covering most of the Indian subcontinent. He also defeated Seleucus Nicator, a general of Alexander the Great, and gained control over parts of western India. His reign is known for administrative efficiency and economic prosperity.

Extra Facts:
Chandragupta Maurya made Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) his capital. He established the Mauryan Empire as the first pan-Indian empire. Arthashastra, written by Chanakya, is a key political treatise from this period. Chandragupta later embraced Jainism, renounced his throne, and fasted to death at Shravanabelagola.

These provinces had their own capitals, including Taxila (North-Western Province) and Ujjain (Western Province). Taxila was a major center of education and trade, while Ujjain was the principal city of the Malwa region. Evidence of these provincial capitals is found in Ashoka's edicts and Buddhist texts.

Extra Facts:
Ashoka divided his empire into four major provinces:
1. Uttarapatha (Taxila),
2. Avanti (Ujjain),
3. Kalinga (Tosali), and
4. Dakshinapatha (Suvarnagiri).

Chandragupta Maurya's teacher was Kautilya (also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta). Kautilya was a renowned political strategist, economist, and philosopher who authored the treatise 'Arthashastra'. He played a pivotal role in helping Chandragupta overthrow the oppressive Nanda dynasty ruler, Dhanananda, and establish the Mauryan Empire. Using his diplomatic and military strategies, Chanakya guided Chandragupta to become the first emperor of a unified India.

Extra Facts:
Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta’s court. He wrote 'Indica', which provides valuable insights into Mauryan India. Kautilya’s Arthashastra is considered one of the most important ancient political texts, covering governance, economics, and warfare strategies.

The foundation of Sanchi Stupa was laid by which of the following Kings ?

[SSC MTS 2023]

Later, the Shunga and Satavahana dynasties expanded and decorated it.

Extra Facts:
The Sanchi Stupa is located in Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its architecture showcases exquisite Buddhist art and symbolism. Ashoka sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism, leading to its expansion.

question:
During the Mauryan reign which of the following provinces was considered as the gold mine hub in Karnataka?

[NTPC CBT 2]

Ujjayini
Taxila
Suvarnagiri

Solution: Correct Answer is Suvarnagiri

Explanation:
During the Mauryan Empire (322-185 BCE), Suvarnagiri was considered the gold mine hub in Karnataka. Located in South India, it was an important economic region under Mauryan administration. The name 'Suvarnagiri' translates to 'Golden Mountain,' reflecting its rich mineral wealth. Both Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka mentioned Suvarnagiri in their inscriptions. The gold extracted here was used for the empire's economic prosperity and military expenses. Greek ambassador Megasthenes also noted the region's wealth in his accounts.

Extra Facts:
The Mauryan Empire divided its territories into provinces called 'Pradesha' or 'Ahara'. Suvarnagiri's strategic importance lay in its mineral resources, which helped fund Mauryan expansion into South India. The Mauryas established strong administrative control over mining activities to maximize revenue.

Indraprastha

Explanation:
According to Emperor Ashoka's inscriptions (rock and pillar edicts), the major provincial centers of the Magadha Empire were Tosali (eastern India), Ujjayini (western India), and Taxila (northwestern India). Although significant during the Mahabharata era, it had limited administrative importance during the Mauryan period.

Extra Facts:
Ashoka's inscriptions mention Pataliputra as the capital of the Magadha Empire. His reign saw the spread of Buddhism and emphasis on Dhamma (moral conduct). After the Kalinga War (261 BCE), Ashoka renounced violence and communicated his messages to the public through edicts.

question:
After which war, Ashoka abandoned the policy of physical occupation?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Kalinga War
Battle of the Hydaspes
Battle of the Tarain
Magadha-Anga war
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kalinga War

Explanation:
Emperor Ashoka abandoned the policy of physical occupation after the Kalinga War in 261 BCE. This war was a turning point in Ashoka's life, as the massive bloodshed and destruction deeply affected him. Post-war, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and propagated the policy of Dhamma, emphasizing non-violence, tolerance, and morality. He acknowledged the consequences of the war in his edicts and vowed to work for peace and welfare.

Extra Facts:
The Kalinga War was fought in present-day Odisha. Ashoka's 13th Rock Edict describes the war, expressing remorse for the loss of life. After the war, Ashoka initiated Dhamma Yatras (religious tours) and spread Buddhism, influencing regions from India to Sri Lanka.

सम्राट अशोक ने 261 ईसा पूर्व में कलिंग युद्ध के बाद भौतिक अधिग्रहण की नीति को त्याग दिया। यह युद्ध अशोक के जीवन में एक निर्णायक मोड़ था, क्योंकि इसके भीषण नरसंहार और विनाश ने उन्हें गहराई से प्रभावित किया। युद्ध के बाद, अशोक ने बौद्ध धर्म अपनाया और धम्म की नीति का प्रचार किया, जिसमें अहिंसा, सहिष्णुता और नैतिकता पर जोर दिया गया। उन्होंने अपने शिलालेखों में इस युद्ध के परिणामों को स्वीकार किया और शांति तथा मानव कल्याण के लिए काम करने का संकल्प लिया।

question:
Who among the following envoys was sent by Seleucus I to the court of Chandragupta Maurya ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Fa-Hien
Al-Biruni
Megasthenes
Deimachus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Megasthenes

Explanation:
Seleucus I, one of Alexander's successors, signed a treaty with Chandragupta Maurya in 305 BCE. Following this treaty, he sent his envoy Megasthenes to Chandragupta Maurya's court. Megasthenes wrote a book called 'Indica', which provides a detailed account of the Mauryan administration, society, and economy. This text is a crucial source for understanding ancient Indian history.

Extra Facts:
Megasthenes described the grandeur of Pataliputra, the strength of the Mauryan army, and Chandragupta's governance in his work. He also wrote about the Indian caste system, agriculture, and trade. Seleucus gave his daughter Helena in marriage to Chandragupta, strengthening ties between the two empires.

question_hi:
सेल्यूकस प्रथम द्वारा चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के दरबार में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा दूत भेजा गया था ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options_hi: फ़ाह्यान
अल-बरूनी
मेगस्थनीज़
डाइमाचस
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है मेगस्थनीज़

Explanation:
सेल्यूकस प्रथम, जो सिकंदर के उत्तराधिकारियों में से एक था, ने चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के साथ 305 ईसा पूर्व में एक संधि की थी। इस संधि के बाद, उसने अपने राजदूत मेगस्थनीज़ को चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के दरबार में भेजा। मेगस्थनीज़ ने अपनी पुस्तक 'इंडिका' में मौर्य साम्राज्य के प्रशासन, समाज और अर्थव्यवस्था का विस्तृत वर्णन किया है। यह ग्रंथ प्राचीन भारत के इतिहास को समझने के लिए एक महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत है।

Extra Facts:
मेगस्थनीज़ ने अपने ग्रंथ में पाटलिपुत्र की भव्यता, मौर्य सेना की शक्ति और चंद्रगुप्त के शासन प्रबंधन का उल्लेख किया है। उसने भारतीय जाति व्यवस्था, कृषि और व्यापार के बारे में भी लिखा। सेल्यूकस ने चंद्रगुप्त को अपनी बेटी हेलेना से विवाह के लिए दी, जिससे दोनों साम्राज्यों के बीच संबंध मजबूत हुए।
